findings.title: Login predicate NPEs when org-linked IDP has null config
findings.body: In IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java getLoginPredicate() does idp.getConfig().get(...) without a null check. If an IDP linked to an organization has a null config map, calling the predicate throws NullPointerException. The predicate is now called on create/update/remove paths in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider to decide login-cache invalidation, so an admin create/update/remove of such an IDP fails instead of invalidating or skipping invalidation.

findings.title: remove() NPEs when alias does not exist
findings.body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java remove() fetches storedIdp via idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) which is null when the alias does not exist, then unconditionally calls registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp) on the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch. registerIDPInvalidation dereferences idp.getInternalId() and idp.getAlias(), so removing a non-existent alias throws NullPointerException instead of returning false from idpDelegate.remove().

findings.title: getForLogin cache not invalidated by organization lifecycle changes
findings.body: In InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java getForLogin() caches ID sets per realm+FetchMode with organizationId as search key, but invalidation is only registered from IdentityProviderStorageProvider create/update/remove. Organization-level operations that change the login-visible set without touching the IDP model through that provider - e.g. organization disable/enable, organization removal, or direct org membership mapping changes - do not invalidate the .idp.login keys. The cached ID list is then stale and login pages can show IDPs that should be hidden or miss IDPs that should appear until the login keys happen to be invalidated by an unrelated IDP write.
